162	**The one seam this plan touches:** `solve(spec, band, cand) -> SimResult` in
163	`app/sim/rf_adapter.py`, selected by `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve`.
164	Nothing in `orchestrator.py`, `pool.py`, `score.py`, or the agent layer needs
165	to change for the adapter fix itself — that's the point of the seam. §6 adds
166	one small, separate seam (a confirmation call), described there.
167	
168	## 5. How Devin actually "calls tools" (brief)
169	
170	Devin does **not** use a function-calling / native tool-use API the way the
171	Anthropic Messages API does. There is no schema the backend registers with
172	Devin that Devin then invokes structurally. Instead:
173	
174	1. The backend creates one Devin **session** per run (`POST /v3/.../sessions`)
175	   and sends a big **prompt** (`app/agent/prompts.py`) that includes a
176	   `## Protocol` section written in plain English + example JSON: *"each of
177	   your replies must contain exactly one fenced ```json block with ONE
178	   action: simulate | sweep | done | spec"*.
179	2. Devin runs autonomously **inside its own VM** — its own shell, filesystem,
180	   package manager. It can `pip install bpy`, run scripts, read an attached
181	   `.blend` file, and (if `repos: [...]` is set and the org's GitHub
182	   integration can see the repo) follow **Skills** — `SKILL.md` files under
183	   `.agents/skills/` that are auto-discovered and inject procedure ("run
184	   `tools/extract_blend.py` like this"). None of that VM-internal activity
185	   (shell commands, file edits) is visible to the backend as structured
186	   events — it's opaque compute happening on Devin's side.
187	3. The only thing the backend ever sees is **chat messages** Devin posts
188	   back into the session, fetched by polling
189	   `GET /sessions/{id}/messages?after={cursor}` every ~10-30 s
190	   (`DevinAgent._poll_messages` in `app/agent/devin.py`). Devin has no
191	   webhooks; this is deliberate, documented API design on their side.
192	4. `DevinAgent._parse_action` takes the **last fenced ```json block** in each
193	   new Devin-authored message, JSON-decodes it, and validates it against the
194	   `AgentRequest` Pydantic union in `app/models.py`. **That fenced block is
195	   the "tool call"** from the orchestrator's point of view — a
196	   backend-defined wire protocol carried inside ordinary chat text, not a
197	   native Devin tool-calling mechanism. Malformed JSON gets one corrective
198	   message ("your last reply had no valid action...") before falling back.
199	5. `orchestrator.py` executes the parsed action (run FDTD/PyNEC sims in the
200	   process pool, score them, build the evidence report) and sends the result
201	   back as the **next** chat message (`prompts.report_message`). Devin reads
202	   that evidence and replies with its next action. This request/response
203	   loop repeats until a `done` action passes the simulation gate.
204	6. Because `AgentPort` (`app/agent/port.py`) is the same narrow interface for
205	   both `DevinAgent` and the heuristic `MockAgent`, `orchestrator.py` never
206	   has agent-vendor-specific code in it — it just calls `next_action(report)`
207	   and gets back one of `SimulateRequest | SweepRequest | DoneRequest |
208	   SpecRequest`.
209	
210	In short: **Devin's "tools" are backend concepts described in a prompt, not
211	API-registered functions** — the fenced-JSON convention *is* the tool-calling
212	layer, implemented entirely in our parsing code, not Devin's.
213	
214	## 6. Letting the agent search *and* use the real solver (the actual conflict)
215	
216	> ✅ **Decision made, built, and live-verified 2026-08-22: two-tier.** The
217	> mechanism below is implemented exactly as designed — `pool.solve_with()`
218	> (bypasses `SIM_SOLVER` for one explicit call) + `orchestrator._finish()`
219	> calling it once on the winner when `CONFIRM_SOLVER` is set. Verified both
220	> offline (`scripts/selftest.py::test_confirm_winner`, a dependency-free
221	> stub solver at `app/sim/_offline_stub.py`) and live against real openEMS
222	> (`CONFIRM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve`, ~61s, real S11 curve landed in
223	> `run.final["openems_confirmation"]` and in `report.md`'s new "Real-solver
224	> confirmation" section). `run_finished` fires before the confirmation call,
225	> so it never gates or delays the reported result — confirmed by the test
226	> asserting `run.status == "finished"` throughout.
227	
228	Wiring `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve` naively makes the search in §2
229	run at real-FDTD speed: ~2 minutes/candidate instead of milliseconds. A full
230	anchor sweep (4 corners + edges every 18 mm — ~16-20 anchors for a phone-size
231	device) would take **30-60+ minutes** just for one pass, before any
232	`length_mm`/`gap_mm` sweep on top. Against `MAX_WALL_CLOCK_S = 8 * 60` in
233	`orchestrator.py`, that barrier trips after 3-4 candidates total — nowhere
234	near enough breadth for the agent to actually "take over the manual testing"
235	the way it already does with the fast oracle.
236	
237	Cranking `MAX_WALL_CLOCK_S` way up "fixes" this but throws away exactly the
238	property that makes the demo watchable and the loop cheap. **Better fix,
239	already implied by the project's own architecture** (DESIGN.md ADR-3: *"PyNEC
240	in-loop... openEMS demoted to optional confirmation"*; M4 backlog already
241	names, as not yet built, *"openEMS single-shot confirmation of the
242	winner"*): keep the search on the fast solver, and spend the slow solver
243	**once**, at the end, confirming the winner — not on every candidate.
244	
245	**Concrete mechanism:**
246	
247	1. **Leave `SIM_SOLVER` pointed at the bundled fast oracle** (default
248	   `app.sim.oracle:solve`, or the sim team's PyNEC cross-check once it's
249	   installable — see `rf/progress_simulation.md`'s PyNEC/MSVC note) for the
250	   whole agent loop. The agent keeps searching broadly and cheaply, exactly
251	   as already verified in M0/M2.
252	2. **Add a new, separate env**, e.g. `CONFIRM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve`
253	   (unset by default — opt-in, since it needs `rf/.venv` present).
254	3. **Add one `pool.solve_with(solver_spec, spec, band, cand)` function**
255	   (small addition to `app/sim/pool.py`) that resolves and runs a solver by
256	   name **on demand**, instead of always reading the process-wide
257	   `SIM_SOLVER` env — everything else about the process pool (isolation,
258	   async dispatch) stays the same.
259	4. **In `orchestrator._finish()`** (`app/runs/orchestrator.py`), after the
260	   `ranking` is decided but before `run_finished` is emitted: if
261	   `CONFIRM_SOLVER` is set and a winner exists, call
262	   `pool.solve_with(CONFIRM_SOLVER, run.spec, band_for(run, winner), winner)`
263	   with a **generous, separate timeout** (real FDTD minutes, not the
264	   interactive loop's budget — this call is off the critical path, it's the
265	   very last thing before reporting). Attach the result as a new artifact,
266	   e.g. `openems_confirmation`, alongside the existing `agent_report`
267	   addendum — **never a gate**: if it fails (no `rf/.venv` on this machine,
268	   openEMS crash, timeout), the run still finishes with the oracle-based
269	   ranking and simply notes the confirmation didn't run, mirroring exactly
270	   how `agent_report` already degrades today.
271	5. This gives you, honestly, both things the user is asking for at once:
272	   the agent still autonomously walks the whole candidate space the way an
273	   RF engineer would (fast oracle, in-loop, already proven), *and* the
274	   headline number that ships in the report is checked against the real
275	   physics-accurate FDTD solver (slow, but only paid once per run).
276	
277	If, instead, the actual intent is *"I want the agent's in-loop reasoning to
278	be based on real FDTD numbers, not the oracle's,"* that's a different,
279	harder ask — it means shrinking the anchor grid drastically (e.g. corners
280	only, no edge points) and accepting a much shallower search per run. Worth
281	an explicit decision before building; the confirmation-step approach above
282	is the one that doesn't force that trade-off. Flag which one is wanted
283	before §8 starts.
284	
285	## 7. Where to place new engineering rules
286	
287	A recurring question as this gets built out further: when a new placement or
288	antenna-design rule comes up, where does it belong? The codebase already
289	draws this line in a few places — worth keeping consistent rather than
290	picking ad hoc per rule:
291	
292	| Kind of rule | Example | Lives in | Why there |
293	|---|---|---|---|
294	| **Hard physical/geometric constraint** — not a judgment call, either it's buildable/correct or it isn't | IFA arm must run beside the ground plane, not above it (image-current cancellation); arm direction derived from board interior, not the raw feed/short offset | `rf/geometry.py` (what the solver is even allowed to construct) | Enforced deterministically at the geometry-building layer; never left to the agent or the LLM to get right by accident |
295	| **Candidate-position search space** — which spots exist to be proposed at all | perimeter anchors, corner-first, spacing_mm | `app/geometry/spec.py::make_anchors()` | This *is* the "candidate generation layer" (deep-research §5); device-derived, computed once per spec, not per-run config |
296	| **Hard pre-screen / keep-out check** — reject a spot before ever simulating it | distance to nearest metal ≥ band's `clearance_mm` | `app/geometry/spec.py::clearance_at()`, consumed by both anchor annotation and `score.py` diffs | Cheap, deterministic, geometry-only — no need to burn a simulation to learn this |
297	| **Deterministic engineering hint** — arithmetic diagnosis of a completed simulation | "resonance 2.62 GHz vs 2.44 → arm ~7% short"; "R=18Ω too low → increase gap_mm" | `app/sim/score.py::hints_for()` | Explicit design principle already in the code's own docstring: *"Hints are deterministic physics arithmetic — never LLM."* Keep it that way; a new hint is a new `if` branch here, not prompt text |
298	| **Narrative rule of thumb** — background knowledge the agent should keep in mind while reasoning, not a computed fact about one candidate | "λ/4 monopole rarely fits a phone edge — prefer IFA/meander"; "corners clear in two directions" | `app/agent/prompts.py::ANTENNA_NOTES` | This is the free-text "playbook" injected into the create prompt — advisory, not gated; the right place for anything you'd say out loud to a junior RF engineer once, not check in code |
299	| **Convergence / stopping policy** — when is a design "good enough" | how many iterations, when to stop refining | Nowhere in the backend, deliberately — the agent's own judgment (ADR-5) | *"Agent decides convergence; orchestrator enforces only the simulation gate"* — a deliberate architecture decision (DESIGN.md ADR-5), not an oversight. Do not add a `max_iterations` here without revisiting that ADR first |
300	| **Which solver runs when** (fast search vs. slow confirmation) | oracle for search, real FDTD once at the end | `SIM_SOLVER` / `CONFIRM_SOLVER` env selection + `orchestrator._finish()` (see §6, new) | Budget-driven infrastructure choice, not engineering judgment — the backend should own it outright, the agent shouldn't need to reason about which solver it's talking to |
301	
302	Rule of thumb for a new rule you're adding: **"is this true regardless of
303	which candidate we're looking at, or computed from one candidate's
304	result?"** — the former goes in `spec.py`/`geometry.py` (search-space /
305	hard-constraint layer), the latter in `score.py` (per-result hints) unless
306	it's genuinely advisory background knowledge, in which case it goes in
307	`prompts.py::ANTENNA_NOTES` as prose for the agent to reason with.
308

14	import run_simulation` would raise ModuleNotFoundError the instant this ran
15	inside the backend's own interpreter (in the ProcessPoolExecutor, that's the
16	same interpreter as the parent process) -- there is no way to install
17	openEMS into the backend's venv without an ABI mismatch. So `solve()` below
18	shells out to rf/.venv's python via `rf/cli.py` (stdin JSON in, result JSON
19	written to a --out file -- **not stdout**: openEMS's C++ engine writes its
20	own verbose progress logging directly to the process's stdout, confirmed by
21	running it for real, so a JSON result can't reliably share that stream).
22	Same subprocess-to-a-separate-interpreter pattern `app/geometry/extract.py`
23	already uses for the bpy/Python-3.11 boundary; same file-not-stdout handoff
24	that script already uses for the same reason (bpy's own console spam).
25	
26	Mapping notes (keep in sync with rf/models.py):
27	- their Candidate dataclass rejects unknown keys -> only the types.ts fields
28	  are forwarded (anchor_id / band_id / prior / rationale / params stay here).
29	- their IFA builder reads the pin height from feed_point_mm.z (0 -> default),
30	  so our `params.height_mm` is mapped onto it.
31	- `device.manifest_path` -> the device's geometry.json (same manifest shape
32	  their blend_loader writes: parts[].{node_path, material_key, eps_r,
33	  sigma_S_per_m, bbox_mm, stl_path}); `device.board.size_mm` is the device
34	  outline; `device.components` is our classified list for when their step 6
35	  (real materials) lands.
36	- their result has no input impedance -> ours stays (0, 0) and the scorer
37	  skips the impedance hints.
38	- `SIM_OPTS` env (JSON) passes solver knobs, e.g.
39	  {"mesh_res": "coarse", "boundary": "MUR", "freq_points": 21}.
40	
41	Env: `RF_PYTHON` overrides the interpreter (default: `rf/.venv/Scripts/python.exe`
42	on Windows, `rf/.venv/bin/python` elsewhere); `RF_TIMEOUT_S` overrides the
43	subprocess timeout (default 600s -- FDTD solves run minutes, not the
44	oracle's milliseconds).
45	"""
46	from __future__ import annotations
47	
48	import json
49	import os
50	import subprocess
51	import tempfile
52	import time
53	from pathlib import Path
54	
55	from app.models import BandRequirement, Candidate, DeviceSpec, S11Point, SimResult
56	
57	REPO_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
58	DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S = 600.0
59	
60	
61	def _rf_python() -> Path | None:
62	    """Resolve an openEMS-capable interpreter. Never assumes -- returns None
63	    (not a guess) if nothing is found, so the caller can fail with a clear
64	    message instead of a confusing ModuleNotFoundError two layers down."""
65	    if py := os.environ.get("RF_PYTHON"):
66	        p = Path(py)
67	        return p if p.exists() else None
68	    for candidate in (REPO_DIR / "rf" / ".venv" / "Scripts" / "python.exe",  # Windows
69	                     REPO_DIR / "rf" / ".venv" / "bin" / "python"):          # posix
70	        if candidate.exists():
71	            return candidate
72	    return None
73	
74	
75	def build_config(spec: DeviceSpec, band: BandRequirement, cand: Candidate) -> dict:
76	    feed = list(cand.feed_point_mm)
77	    if "height_mm" in cand.params:
78	        feed[2] = float(cand.params["height_mm"])
79	    device: dict = {
80	        "device_id": spec.device_id,
81	        "name": spec.name,
82	        "board": {"size_mm": list(spec.board.size_mm), "stackup": spec.board.stackup,
83	                  "epsilon_r": spec.board.epsilon_r,
84	                  "loss_tangent": spec.board.loss_tangent},
85	        "enclosure": spec.enclosure.model_dump(),
86	        "components": [c.model_dump() for c in spec.components],
87	    }
88	    if spec.geometry_path:
89	        device["manifest_path"] = spec.geometry_path
90	    return {
91	        "candidate": {
92	            "candidate_id": cand.candidate_id,
93	            "antenna_type": cand.antenna_type,
94	            "position_mm": list(cand.position_mm),
95	            "feed_point_mm": feed,
96	            "length_mm": cand.length_mm,
97	            "orientation": cand.orientation,
98	        },
99	        "band": {
100	            "id": band.id, "f_low_ghz": band.f_low_ghz, "f_high_ghz": band.f_high_ghz,
101	            "s11_db_max": band.s11_db_max, "efficiency_min": band.efficiency_min,
102	        },
103	        "device": device,
104	        "sim": json.loads(os.environ.get("SIM_OPTS", "{}")),
105	    }
106	
107	
108	def from_result(cand: Candidate, out: dict, t0: float) -> SimResult:
109	    curve = [S11Point(f_ghz=round(float(p["f_ghz"]), 4), s11_db=round(float(p["s11_db"]), 2))
110	             for p in out.get("s11_curve", [])]
111	    return SimResult(
112	        candidate_id=cand.candidate_id,
113	        status=out.get("status", "failed"),
114	        runtime_s=round(float(out.get("runtime_s") or (time.perf_counter() - t0)), 3),
115	        s11_curve=curve,
116	        s11_min_db=round(float(out.get("s11_min_db", 0.0)), 2),
117	        resonant_ghz=round(float(out.get("resonant_ghz", 0.0)), 4),
118	        bandwidth_mhz=round(float(out.get("bandwidth_mhz", 0.0)), 1),
119	        efficiency=round(float(out.get("efficiency", 0.0)), 3),
120	        peak_gain_dbi=round(float(out.get("peak_gain_dbi", 0.0)), 2),
121	        vswr=round(min(float(out.get("vswr") or 99.0), 99.0), 2),
122	        impedance_ohm=tuple(out.get("impedance_ohm", (0.0, 0.0))),
123	        meets_requirements=bool(out.get("meets_requirements", False)),
124	        notes=f"[rf.run_simulation] {out.get('notes', '')}",
125	    )
126	
127	
128	def solve(spec: DeviceSpec, band: BandRequirement, cand: Candidate) -> SimResult:
129	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
130	    py = _rf_python()
131	    if py is None:
132	        return SimResult(candidate_id=cand.candidate_id, status="failed",
133	                         runtime_s=round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3),
134	                         notes="rf/.venv not found (set RF_PYTHON to an "
135	                               "openEMS-capable Python 3.11 interpreter)")
136	    timeout_s = float(os.environ.get("RF_TIMEOUT_S", DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S))
137	    cfg_json = json.dumps(build_config(spec, band, cand))
138	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rf_solve_") as tmpdir:
139	        out_path = Path(tmpdir) / "result.json"
140	        try:
141	            proc = subprocess.run(
142	                [str(py), "-m", "rf.cli", "--out", str(out_path)], input=cfg_json,
143	                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout_s, cwd=str(REPO_DIR))
144	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
145	            return SimResult(candidate_id=cand.candidate_id, status="failed",
146	                             runtime_s=round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3),
147	                             notes=f"rf.cli timed out after {timeout_s:.0f}s")
148	        except OSError as e:  # interpreter vanished/unrunnable between check and exec
149	            return SimResult(candidate_id=cand.candidate_id, status="failed",
150	                             runtime_s=round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3),
151	                             notes=f"rf.cli could not be started: {e}")
152	        if proc.returncode != 0 or not out_path.exists():
153	            # openEMS/CSXCAD write their own progress logging straight to
154	            # stdout, interleaved with anything Python prints -- neither
155	            # stream is reliably a clean error message, but it's all we have
156	            tail = "\n".join((proc.stderr or proc.stdout).strip().splitlines()[-12:])
157	            return SimResult(candidate_id=cand.candidate_id, status="failed",
158	                             runtime_s=round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3),
159	                             notes=f"rf.cli failed (rc={proc.returncode}): "
160	                                   f"{tail or '(no output)'}")
161	        try:
162	            out = json.loads(out_path.read_text())
163	        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
164	            return SimResult(candidate_id=cand.candidate_id, status="failed",
165	                             runtime_s=round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3),
166	                             notes=f"rf.cli result file invalid JSON: {e}")
167	    return from_result(cand, out, t0)
168

1	"""Process-pool execution of the simulation boundary.
2	
3	THE SIM SEAM (DESIGN.md §7): simulation is the sim workstream's subsystem, not
4	ours. Our contract with it is exactly one callable:
5	
6	    solve(spec: DeviceSpec, band: BandRequirement, cand: Candidate) -> SimResult
7	
8	Point SIM_SOLVER at any "module:function" honouring that contract (default:
9	our bundled reference oracle, app.sim.oracle:solve) and the backend uses it —
10	no code changes here. Process isolation stays either way: solver crashes are
11	contained, C extensions can't stall the event loop."""
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import asyncio
15	import importlib
16	import os
17	from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
18	
19	from app.models import BandRequirement, Candidate, DeviceSpec, SimResult
20	
21	_pool: ProcessPoolExecutor | None = None
22	
23	
24	def _resolve_solver(solver_spec: str | None = None):
25	    spec = solver_spec or os.environ.get("SIM_SOLVER", "app.sim.oracle:solve")
26	    mod_name, fn_name = spec.split(":")
27	    return getattr(importlib.import_module(mod_name), fn_name)
28	
29	
30	def _worker(spec_json: str, band_json: str, cand_json: str,
31	           solver_spec: str | None = None) -> str:
32	    # runs in a child process — import here keeps parent import time down
33	    solve = _resolve_solver(solver_spec)
34	    spec = DeviceSpec.model_validate_json(spec_json)
35	    band = BandRequirement.model_validate_json(band_json)
36	    cand = Candidate.model_validate_json(cand_json)
37	    return solve(spec, band, cand).model_dump_json()
38	
39	
40	def start_pool(workers: int = 4) -> None:
41	    global _pool
42	    if _pool is None:
43	        _pool = ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers)
44	
45	
46	def shutdown_pool() -> None:
47	    global _pool
48	    if _pool is not None:
49	        _pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)
50	        _pool = None
51	
52	
53	async def solve_async(spec: DeviceSpec, band: BandRequirement,
54	                      cand: Candidate) -> SimResult:
55	    """Solve one candidate with whatever SIM_SOLVER names (the process-wide
56	    default -- the in-loop search)."""
57	    return await _run(spec, band, cand, None)
58	
59	
60	async def solve_with(solver_spec: str, spec: DeviceSpec, band: BandRequirement,
61	                     cand: Candidate) -> SimResult:
62	    """Solve one candidate with an EXPLICIT solver, bypassing SIM_SOLVER --
63	    e.g. a one-off real-FDTD confirmation of the agent's winner after a
64	    fast-oracle search concludes (integration plan §6: the in-loop search
65	    stays cheap; the real solver is spent once, on the result that's about
66	    to ship). Same process pool, same isolation/crash containment as the
67	    regular search path."""
68	    return await _run(spec, band, cand, solver_spec)
69	
70	
71	async def _run(spec: DeviceSpec, band: BandRequirement, cand: Candidate,
72	               solver_spec: str | None) -> SimResult:
73	    assert _pool is not None, "pool not started"
74	    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
75	    try:
76	        raw = await loop.run_in_executor(
77	            _pool, _worker, spec.model_dump_json(), band.model_dump_json(),
78	            cand.model_dump_json(), solver_spec)
79	        return SimResult.model_validate_json(raw)
80	    except Exception as e:  # BrokenProcessPool et al.
81	        return SimResult(candidate_id=cand.candidate_id, status="failed",
82	                         notes=f"pool failure: {e}")
83
